Hi Maria / Security team,

Answers below — I’ve attached our current retention policy PDF and a CSV schema sample for exported archives. See attachments: redwood-audit-retention-policy.pdf, audit_export_schema.csv.

1) Default retention (Hosted API)
- Audit logs (administrative events, configuration changes): 365 days by default for Hosted customers.
- Access logs (API request metadata / token-level events): 90 days by default.
- Note: Dedicated & Private deployments can configure longer local retention via config (we've seen customers keep audit logs 3–7+ years for compliance).

2) Export capabilities
- Exports: daily archive (compressed .jsonl or .csv) or streaming export (Kafka/HTTP) to customer endpoints.
- S3 delivery: we support scheduled delivery to a customer-owned S3 bucket (AWS, GCP Storage, Azure Blob) using an IAM role or signed URLs. Files are delivered encrypted in transit (TLS) and encrypted at rest when in the destination bucket (customer-managed keys supported).
- Export schema: see attached audit_export_schema.csv for field names and types.

3) Residency
- Hosted: logs are stored in the region of the account by default (US or EU). For EU residency, we keep data in EU zones and the export endpoints can be restricted to EU endpoints.
- Dedicated/Private: full control — logs remain in customer VPC/on-prem.

4) PII & redaction
- Exports include identifiers used in logs (user_id, session_id), but we do not export raw request payloads by default.
- Redaction: we offer export-time field redaction (remove or hash specific fields) and column-level encryption. Redaction rules can be applied during export (configurable via export-instructions.md).

5) Deletion and retention enforcement
- Deletion API: customers can request immediate deletion of specific log ranges (subject to legal hold).
- Automated retention enforcement runs daily; expired data is purged according to policy.

If you want, we can set up a 30-minute call next week to walk through a sample export and S3 setup.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Audit & Access logs — residency/retention/export Qs

Hi Maria — quick clarifications:

- Credential rotation: We prefer customers to own the target bucket and provision an IAM role that Redwood can assume. Alternatively, we can accept short-lived signed URLs for each delivery. We do not recommend long-lived secret keys. We rotate our own service credentials regularly and can demonstrate rotation logs during the call.

- Pseudonymization: Our redaction options include reversible masking (for troubleshooting) and non-reversible hashing (SHA-256 with a per-customer salt stored in the customer control-plane). The per-customer salt is not derivable from the export, so hashes are practically irreversible for external auditors. We can also offer HMAC-based formats on request.

- Historical exports: If data was retained (e.g., audit logs kept for >90 days because you are on Dedicated or had a retention override), we can export historical data. For Hosted accounts with default 90-day access-log retention, data older than 90 days may already have been purged. However, we can check your account retention history and run a backfill export if the data still exists in our cold storage — we recommend doing this ASAP while we verify.

Export instructions (snippet):
- Create a customer-owned bucket (preferably with server-side encryption enabled).
- Provide an IAM role ARN with put-object/write permissions or generate pre-signed upload URLs.
- Send desired export window and redaction rules to ops@redwood.ai.
- Ops will schedule a test delivery; once validated, we can make it recurring daily/weekly.

Docs: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/retention-guide (see "Scheduled exports" section).

— Mateo Alvarez
Platform Operations
